title: Dancing Demon at the Noh Mask Mansion
notes: Detective-cast (Conan, Kogoro, Ran, Inspector Megure, Officer Takagi) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old cases/ file badly undercounted the case: it listed only one victim (Akaza) and treated the museum executive/manager/receptionist purely as background 'suspects' with generic `knows` edges, when the transcript shows all three (Mibu, Nagata, Seikanji) are a secret inheritance-murder conspiracy against curator Izumi, and the true culprit Hatsuho Toba (Izumi's nurse, and Mibu's estranged half-sister) murders all three of them plus Akaza, tries to murder Izumi himself (he survives -- the old file omits this entirely, never listing Izumi as a victim/target), and frames the dead Mibu for the attack on Izumi to fabricate a self-defense story, using a fake phone call and a demon mask sighted through a window as staged evidence. The old file's `s4`->`v1` murderer/victim pair is directionally correct (Toba did kill Akaza) but the case is really 4 murders + 1 attempted murder, not 1. Old file also collapsed the killing of Seikanji and Nagata into a single vague 'stabs the other two conspirators' event without naming a mechanism; transcript instead shows Toba improvising two different fake-weapon tricks (poisoned spoon underside; two skewers clamped with carved wood chips to fake a chisel wound) that are the actual solvable clues. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The 'call to police' and the later 'Stop it, Sis!' call both went out on the same internal-only extension -- the first faked by Mibu to stall, the second faked by Toba (after Mibu was already dead) to fabricate a timeline where Mibu was still alive attacking Izumi.

Izumi's wound looks chisel-shaped, but no chisel is missing -- only Toba's paired skewers, clamped into a V by her hand-carved wood chips, reproduce that exact cross-section, proving the 'chisel attack' pinned on Mibu was staged.
